title: Vacuum polarization and renormalized stress-energy tensor of spherical thin shells
authors: Julio Arrechea, Cormac Breen, Adrian Ottewill, Lorenzo Pisani, Peter Taylor
abstract: We provide a thorough study of the properties of the Boulware vacuum in the spacetime of a spherical, static thin shell with a Minkowski interior. To this end, we calculate the renormalized vacuum polarization and stress-energy tensor of massless scalar fields via the extended-coordinate prescription, paying particular attention to their scaling as the shell approaches the black hole limit. Near the surface of the thin shell, we obtain the expected leading-order singular behavior of both quantities via two independent methods: a high-frequency approximation for the modes, and a weak-field approximation. At the center of the shell we find non-local, Casimir-like contributions that remain finite in the black hole limit, and whose backreaction effects we compute via the semiclassical Einstein equations. Away from these regions amenable to analytic treatment, we obtain numerical results for a wide range of shell compactnesses and field couplings. In the black hole limit, we show that the vacuum polarization and renormalized stress-energy tensor outside the shell quickly approach the ones generated by a Schwarzschild black hole, suggesting a possible universality in the vacuum outside highly compact horizonless objects. This work addresses the conceptual and technical aspects necessary for computing renormalized expectation values in matter configurations, laying the foundations for future explorations on the subject.
summary: This paper provides a detailed theoretical investigation into how quantum fields behave near a spherical thin shell. By calculating the renormalized stress-energy tensor, it addresses technical challenges in curved spacetime QFT and suggests that vacuum effects outside highly compact objects might exhibit universal behavior resembling those of a Schwarzschild black hole.
main_problem: The study calculates the renormalized vacuum polarization and stress-energy tensor for quantum fields in the curved spacetime generated by a spherical, static thin shell.
main_result: The calculations show that outside the shell, the vacuum observables approach those of a Schwarzschild black hole in the appropriate limit, suggesting a universality principle.
method: The authors employ advanced techniques including the extended-coordinate prescription and mode-sum renormalization to handle divergences in curved spacetime quantum field theory.
model_or_system: The system is a spherical thin shell separating a Minkowski interior from an exterior geometry that approaches a black hole background. The fields considered are massless scalar fields.
key_observables: Renormalized vacuum polarization (RVP) and the renormalized stress-energy tensor ($\langle \hat{T}_{\alpha eta} angle^{	ext{ren}}$).
important_parameters: Shell compactness, field couplings, and the approach to the black hole limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations like the weak-field expansion near the shell surface and assumes the validity of the extended-coordinate prescription for renormalization.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism using the extended-coordinate method, analyzes singular behavior near the shell surface using multiple approximation techniques, computes non-local Casimir-like contributions at the center, and finally applies semiclassical Einstein equations to compute backreaction effects.
why_interesting: While focused on general relativity/QFT in curved spacetime, the rigorous handling of vacuum expectation values and renormalization procedures is foundational for understanding quantum field theory near boundaries or horizons, which has parallels in open quantum systems.
